task.title: Using at() for rotation at supports
task.body:
Hi Colin. Firstly - thanks for pyCBA. I've started building it into a workflow specific for field testing. Working out which test vehicles to use, quickly exploring expected results for different scenarios, helping define sensor locations based on expected signals, etc.. It's been a good way to speed up the preparation for tests.

In the process I ran into an issue how rotation comes back using [at()](https://ccaprani.github.io/pycba/_modules/pycba/results.html#BeamResults.at), at a support. Understand it is to do with the padding for the bending moment and shear diagrams.
The same thing as what is handled for deflection by deflection_curve() 

To reproduce:
```
import pycba as cba

L=10.0
P=100.0
EI = 30 * 10e9 * 1e-6

beam_analysis = cba.BeamAnalysis([L], EI, supports=["pinned", "roller"])
beam_analysis.set_loads([[1, 2, P, L/2, 0]])
beam_analysis.analyze()

print(beam_analysis.at(0.0)["R"]) # (padded endpoint, = rotation *EI)

r = beam_analysis.beam_results.results
print(r.R[0], r.R[1])       
print(P*L**2 / (16*EI))
```

Fix -
My own workaround has been a function like deflection_curve() but for rotation, which I then interpolate at the position x. Though the same thing could probably be implemented within at() as a small change.
